text:
Someone else pushed commits to `origin/main` after you last fetched, so your local `main` isn't a descendant of the remote tip — Git refuses to push because that would discard their work.

Fix: integrate their commits first, then push.

```
git pull --rebase origin main   # replays your commits on top of theirs
git push
```

If the rebase hits conflicts: resolve, `git add <files>`, `git rebase --continue` (or `git rebase --abort` to back out).

Use `git pull origin main` (merge) instead if your team prefers merge commits, or if your commits are already pushed elsewhere and rewriting them would disrupt others.

Don't use `git push --force` here — it would delete the remote commits.
